title: Ann Arbor Farmers Market Saturday Market Regular Hours
Litter Cleanup at Argo Cascades
description:
Join the Ann Arbor Parks Volunteer Program to help clean up at the beloved and well-used Argo Cascades!
This award-winning amenity sees thousands of people canoeing, kayaking, tubing, and swimming through in the summer. This is an area that is particularly prone to litter accumulation. It needs extra help to keep clean!
During this workday, volunteers will be using trash grabbers and reusable litter collection bags.
Event Details:
  • Date: Monday, September 7th
  • Time: 10:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m.
  • Meeting Location: The Argo Canoe & Kayak Livery.
    • The livery can get very busy, so we encourage carpooling, alternative transport like biking, and trying to get there early.
    • View a map of Argo parking options
What to wear and bring:
  • Long pants, tall socks, and closed-toe shoes
  • Dress for the weather
  • A reusable water bottle
  • We’ll provide tools and supplies
Please note:
  • Volunteers may encounter uneven ground, thorns, poison ivy, and insects like mosquitoes or ticks
  • The litter we find can be absolutely anything and sometimes may include heavy items. Volunteers are instructed to avoid any dangerous items and let park staff know if any are found
  • All minors must have a waiver on file to participate and minors under 14 need to be accompanied by an adult

title: Love a Park w/OSI at Ward Park
description:
Show some love to a city park! Join the City of Ann Arbor’s Office of Sustainability and Innovations and the Ann Arbor Parks Volunteer Program for a volunteer workday focused on caring for the park’s playground area.
To keep the play area safe, we’ll be spreading a fresh layer of play-safe woodchips under and around the equipment using wheelbarrows, pitchforks, and rakes. This task makes a big difference in safety and helps the playground look well cared for.
Whether you’re a longtime volunteer or joining us for the first time, this is a great opportunity to spend time outdoors, connect with community members, and make a visible impact in a neighborhood park.
No prior experience is necessary—staff will provide all tools, supplies, training, and guidance throughout the event.
Come lend a hand, meet your community, and show your love for Ann Arbor Parks!
  •  Date: Friday, September 11, 2026
  •  Time: 3:00 – 5:00 p.m.
  •  Location: Ward Park
What to wear and bring:
  • Closed-toe shoes
  • Weather-appropriate clothes that can get dusty or dirty
  • Reusable water bottle
  • We’ll provide gloves, tools, and instruction
What to expect:
  • This is a physical task involving lifting and moving mulch with shovels and wheelbarrows
  • Work areas may have uneven terrain or minor tripping hazards
  • Volunteers may encounter uneven ground, thorns, poison ivy, and insects like mosquitoes or ticks
  • Minors must be accompanied by a guardian OR have their waiver signed 24 hours in advance to the workday

title: Birding by Boat - Guided Kayaking on the Huron River
description:
Immerse yourself in the natural beauty of Gallup Park from a unique perspective during our Birdwatching by Kayak adventure. This guided class is perfect for both seasoned paddlers and those new to kayaking, as we explore the calm, two-mile stillwater section of Gallup Pond. Cost, $35. For ages 18+. Register here: secure.rec1.com…


While we'll cover very basic paddling techniques, the primary focus of this experience is to guide you through the prime bird habitat of Gallup Pond. An experienced local naturalist, will lead the way, helping you spot and identify various bird species that frequent the Huron River watershed. Keep your eyes peeled for herons, kingfishers, various ducks, and perhaps even an osprey or bald eagle.

title: A²ZERO Green Fair – Kid's Zone Volunteers
description:
Help create a fun, engaging space for kids and families at the A2ZERO Green Fair!
Ann Arbor Parks is looking for  a small team of volunteers to support the Kid’s Zone at the A2ZERO Green Fair. Volunteers will help get the activity area ready before the event begins, assist families and children with activities throughout the evening, and help pack everything up when the fair ends.
Volunteer Shift: 4:30–8:30 p.m.
Public Event: 5:00–8:00 p.m.
You might help by:
  • Setting up Kid’s Zone activities and supplies
  • Welcoming children and families
  • Helping participants with activities
  • Keeping activity areas organized and stocked
  • Assisting staff wherever an extra hand is needed
  • Packing up supplies and helping with cleanup after the event
We only need three volunteers for this role, so each person will be an important part of keeping the Kid’s Zone welcoming, organized, and fun.
Assignments may shift throughout the event, so thank you in advance for bringing a flexible, positive attitude.
Shift Commitment
Please plan to stay for the full 4:30–8:30 p.m. shift, including setup and cleanup. If you’d like to help but cannot stay for the entire shift, please email volunteer@a2gov.org so we can coordinate.
What to Bring
  • Comfortable clothing and shoes
  • Reusable water bottle
We’ll provide a volunteer T-shirt, instructions, activity materials, and everything you need to support the Kid’s Zone.

title: Ann Arbor Farmers Market Saturday Market Regular Hours
Scarlett Mitchell - Invasive Shrub Cutting
description:
As caretakers of Ann Arbor’s Natural Areas, volunteers with the Ann Arbor Parks Department serve the greater community by:
  • Restoring local ecosystems
  • Expanding access to quality experiences in nature
  • Strengthening bonds through service
At this event, you’ll help protect Ann Arbor’s biodiversity and public lands by cutting and removing invasive shrubs with hand saws and loppers. This work creates more space for native plants to thrive, providing food and habitat for birds, pollinators, and other wildlife.
Event Details
  • Date: Saturday, September 19, 2026
  • Time: 9:00 a.m. – 12:00 p.m.
  • Meeting Location: TBD
What You’ll Be Doing
  • Using hand saws and loppers to cut invasive shrubs
  • Hauling brush and working off-trail
  • Supporting the long-term health of this natural area
Hazards & Safety Notes
This work involves the usual hazards of being in nature, including:
  • Off-trail walking on uneven surfaces and difficult footing
  • Exposure to plants with thorns and poison ivy
  • Muddy and hot conditions, depending on weather
  • Expect to get dirty while working outdoors
  • All minors under 14 must be accompanied by a guardian
What to Bring
  • Thick, long pants to protect against ticks and thorny plants
  • Closed-toe shoes (sturdy boots recommended)
  • Dress for the weather, likely hot and sunny, sun protection recommended
  • Filled water bottle
We Provide
  • Tools (hand saws, loppers), gloves, and training
  • Guidance from experienced staff
  • A chance to enjoy time in nature while giving back to your community
 More information: How to prepare for a NAP workday (PDF).

Join the Ann Arbor Parks Volunteer Program and the UM Electric Vehicle Center for a canoe-based clean-up on Gallup Pond, a calm, scenic stretch of the Huron River that is ideal for first-time paddlers.

title: Turnberry Park Workday
description:
Show some love to Turnberry Park! Join the Girl Up Michigan and the Ann Arbor Parks Volunteer Program for a volunteer workday focused on caring for the park’s playground area.
Turnberrry Park is an over eight-acre park off Packard on Turnberry Drive in the southeast corner of the city. This is a relatively large neighborhood park with a playground and picnic tables. The park serves as a green buffer between the neighborhood and US-23. 
During this event, volunteers will focus on weeding under and around the playground equipment. This hands-on work helps keep the play area cleaner, safer, and more welcoming for children, families, and neighbors who visit the park throughout the season.
This is a great opportunity to spend time outdoors, connect with community members, and make a visible impact in a neighborhood park.
No prior experience is necessary—staff will provide all tools, supplies, training, and guidance throughout the event.
Come lend a hand, meet your community, and show your love for Turnberry Park!
  •  Date: Friday, September 25, 2026
  •  Time: 4:30-6:30 pm
  •  Location: Turnberry park
    • Meeting Spot: Playground on Turnberry Lane across from Weeburn Street
What to wear and bring:
  • Closed-toe shoes
  • Weather-appropriate clothes that can get dusty or dirty
  • Reusable water bottle
  • We’ll provide gloves, tools, and instruction
What to expect:
  • Tasks may involve bending, kneeling, pulling weeds, or working close to the ground
  • Work will be outdoors and there may be limited shade
  • All minors must be accompanied by a guardian

title: Ann Arbor Farmers Market Saturday Market Regular Hours
Brokaw - Invasive Shrub Cutting
description:
As caretakers of Ann Arbor’s Natural Areas, volunteers with the Ann Arbor Parks Department serve the greater community by:
  • Restoring local ecosystems
  • Expanding access to quality experiences in nature
  • Strengthening bonds through service
At this event, you’ll help protect Ann Arbor’s biodiversity and public lands by cutting and removing invasive shrubs with hand saws and loppers. This work creates more space for native plants to thrive, providing food and habitat for birds, pollinators, and other wildlife.
Event Details
  • Date: Sunday, September 27, 2026
  • Time: 1:00–4:00 p.m.
  • Location: Brokaw Nature Area
  • Meeting Point: The main entrance on Huron River Drive. 
    • Parking: There a small parking area off of Huron River Drive, marked by a mailbox. We encourage carpooling and using public transportation, whenever possible.
What You’ll Be Doing
  • Using hand saws and loppers to cut invasive shrubs
  • Hauling brush and working off-trail
  • Supporting the long-term health of this natural area
Hazards & Safety Notes
This work involves the usual hazards of being in nature, including:
  • Off-trail walking on uneven surfaces and difficult footing
  • Exposure to plants with thorns and poison ivy
  • Muddy conditions, depending on weather
  • Expect to get dirty while working outdoors
What to Bring
  • Thick, long pants
  • Closed-toe shoes (sturdy boots recommended)
  • Layers to dress for the weather
  • Filled water bottle
We Provide
  • Tools (hand saws, loppers), gloves, and training
  • Guidance from experienced staff
  • A chance to enjoy time in nature while giving back to your community

title: Public Works and Solid Waste Open House
description:
Public Works and Solid Waste Open House
Saturday, Oct. 3, 2026 from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m.
Get ready to roll into the world of Ann Arbor public works!
Join us for a free, family-friendly event where you can explore the tools, vehicles, and people that keep Ann Arbor running smoothly.
Enjoy hands-on activities and demos to discover:
  • How city crews maintain and repair underground water pipes
  • The techniques used to care for and trim our city’s trees
  • How potholes are filled and roads repaired
  • The equipment that collects trash, recycling, and compost from homes and businesses
  • Tips and insights on Ann Arbor’s composting and recycling programs
Bring the whole family to meet our crews, climb aboard the big trucks, and see how we maintain our city while building a sustainable future!
